features.name: Point–segment dependent construction
steps: Open a blank Geometry
Create three independent points A, B, C
Use the Segment tool to connect A-B and B-C
Drag the shared endpoint B to a new position
Both segments must update together and continue to share the same endpoint
Delete A-B
B-C and the remaining objects among the three points continue to exist
features.expected: When dragging the shared endpoint B both segments must update together and continue to share the same endpoint; after deleting A-B, B-C and the remaining objects continue to exist.

features.name: Dynamic center–radius construction
steps: Create center A and radius control point B
Use the Circle tool to create a circle through B
Then create a point C on the circle
Drag B to change the circle radius
The circle, point C on the circle, and all dependent objects update in real time
Move the whole center A
Keep the radius relationship and object dependencies unchanged
features.expected: When dragging the radius control point to change the radius, the circle and the point on it update in real time; after moving the center the radius relationship and object dependencies are unchanged.

features.name: Dynamic angle measurement
steps: Create three points A-B-C and form two segments sharing B
Use the Angle tool to measure ∠ABC
Show the angle value
Drag A or C to change the included angle
The angle value is recomputed in real time
Keep dragging so the angle passes through acute, right, and obtuse states
Measurements always correspond to the current geometric construction
features.expected: The angle value must be recomputed in real time while dragging; when passing through acute/right/obtuse states the measurement always corresponds to the current geometric construction.

features.name: Dynamic polygon editing
steps: Use the Polygon tool to create a quadrilateral
Keep the vertices, edges, and filled area
Drag two of the vertices to change the shape
Verify that the polygon stays closed and the filled area updates in real time
Move other vertices in the same construction
No broken edges or extra vertices are produced
After deleting one polygon object verify that unrelated geometric objects are unaffected
features.expected: After dragging a vertex the polygon must stay closed and the filled area update in real time; no broken edges or extra vertices are produced; after deletion unrelated objects are unaffected.

features.name: Geometric intersection dependency chain
steps: Create two intersecting circles or a line and a circle
Use intersection construction to obtain the intersection point P
Create another segment from P to another existing point
Move the original center, radius point, or line control point
The intersection point P is recomputed automatically
Segments derived from P move in sync
When the source objects intersect again the dependency chain remains valid. Desmos Geometry supports finding intersections through geometry commands. Desmos Help Center
features.expected: The intersection point must be recomputed automatically when the source objects move; segments derived from the intersection point move in sync; when the source objects intersect again the dependency chain remains valid.

features.name: Distance–perimeter–area linkage
steps: Create a triangle or quadrilateral
Compute the distance between two specified points
Compute the perimeter and area of the polygon
Record the three results
Drag a vertex to change the shape
The distance, perimeter, and area are recomputed at the same time
Move another vertex
All measurements keep referencing the same set of geometric objects rather than creating static copies. The relevant measurement commands are supported by Geometry. Desmos
features.expected: After dragging a vertex the distance / perimeter / area must be recomputed together; measurements always reference the same set of geometric objects rather than static copies.

features.name: Geometry overlaid with functions
steps: Create the function f(x)=x+5·sin(10x)
The corresponding curve appears in the graph
Then use the Geometry tools to create circles, segments, and polygons
Pan or zoom the view
Ensure that function curves and geometric objects coexist in the same coordinate space
Modify the function expression
Only the function curve is recomputed while manually created geometric constructions remain
Then drag a geometric vertex to verify that the two sets of objects can work independently yet simultaneously. Geometry embeds Graphing Calculator capabilities. Desmos Help Center
features.expected: Function curves and geometric objects must coexist in the same coordinate space; modifying the function only recomputes the curve while the geometric construction is preserved; the two sets of objects work independently yet simultaneously.

features.name: Sliders driving geometric relationships
steps: Create the parameter a and generate a slider
Use a in an angle, coordinate, or other geometric expression
Create a point or transformation result that depends on that parameter
Continuously adjust a
All associated geometric objects change in real time
Then drag another base geometric point

Verify that the two input types "slider parameters + geometric control points" jointly drive the final construction instead of turning the object into a static figure. The official examples include slider-driven rotation. Desmos Help Center
features.expected: Slider parameters and geometric control points must jointly drive the final construction; during continuous adjustment all related objects change in real time; it must not degenerate into a static figure.

features.name: Geometric transformation chain
steps: Create a triangle ABC
Apply one rotation or another supported geometric transformation to it
Apply a second transformation to the transformation result
Drag the original vertex A
The original triangle, the first-level result, and the second-level result all update in sync
Modify the transformation parameters
The whole dependency chain is recomputed rather than only the last object being updated. Geometry officially supports transformations. Desmos Help Center
features.expected: The second-level transformation chain must update in sync (the original object plus the two levels of results); after changing the transformation parameters the whole dependency chain is recomputed rather than only the last object being updated.

features.name: Table data coexisting with geometry
steps: Create a table through "Add item"
Enter at least two groups of (x,y) data and display the data points
Create an algebraic function
Then use the Geometry tools to create a circle or segment
Modify one value in the table
The corresponding data point updates while the function and manually created geometric objects are preserved
Drag a geometric object
The table data stays unchanged
features.expected: Modifying a table value only updates the data point, while the function and manually created geometric objects are preserved; dragging a geometric object does not change the table data.

features.name: Image background + mathematical annotations
steps: Insert a local image
Adjust the image center, width, height, or transparency
Create several points and segments on the image as annotations
Add a function curve or a measurement
Move/zoom the image again
The image properties are saved and other independent geometric objects are not accidentally deleted
After saving and reopening the image, annotations, and expressions are still restored
features.expected: After saving the image properties (center / width & height / transparency) the annotations and expressions are not deleted; they are fully restored on reopening.

features.name: A mixed document with notes + tables + geometry
steps: Add a note
Create a table and enter data
Add a function expression
Create at least one circle and one polygon
Use the edit-list function to copy or delete one of the items
Reorder the items
Ensure that deleting a table or note does not destroy geometric constructions that do not depend on it, while derived objects update correctly when the data they depend on is modified
features.expected: Deleting a table or note does not destroy geometric constructions that do not depend on it; when dependent data is modified the derived objects update correctly.

features.name: Object duplication and derived modification
steps: Create a geometric construction
Use the copy function in the expression list to duplicate the relevant items
Modify the copy's parameters or position
The original object stays unchanged
Then modify the base control point of the original object
Only dependency items that still reference the original object change in sync
After deleting the copy the original construction fully exists
features.expected: After copying an object, modifying the copy does not affect the original; when modifying the original only the dependency items that still reference it change in sync; after deleting the copy the original construction fully remains.

features.name: Complex construction + dynamic verification
steps: Create two circles, several points, and segments
Construct at least one intersection point
Form a polygon based on the intersection points
Measure one of the angles and the polygon area
Drag the most upstream center or radius point
Intersections, segments, polygons, angles, and areas are all recomputed automatically
Keep dragging another source point
Verify that the whole dependency graph stays consistent
features.expected: When dragging the most upstream object the intersections / segments / polygons / angles / areas are all recomputed automatically; the whole dependency graph stays consistent.

features.name: Save—close—reopen
steps: Create a mixed Geometry document containing function expressions, geometric figures, measurements, tables, and notes
Save
Rename
Leave the current page and reopen from saved work
Verify that the expressions, graph, object positions, and dependencies are all restored
Then modify a source object and save again
The latest state is still preserved after the second reopening
features.expected: After saving, renaming, and reopening, the expressions/graph/positions and dependency relationships are fully restored; after modifying and saving again the latest state is still preserved.

features.name: Integrated geometry workspace
steps: Start from a blank canvas
Create a quadrilateral
Create a circle centered on one of the vertices
Construct the intersection of the circle with another geometric object
Use intersections to form a second figure
Add angle and distance/area measurements
Add a slider controlling an algebra or transformation parameter
Insert a note explaining the construction
Adjust several source objects
All derived objects and measurements stay dynamically consistent
Save and reopen to verify full restoration
features.expected: When adjusting several source objects in an integrated construction all derived objects and measurements stay dynamically consistent; save and reopen to verify full restoration.

features.name: Auxiliary math keyboard
steps: Open Geometry
Tap the auxiliary keyboard in the bottom-left corner
Expand the math input panel
Use on-screen buttons to enter digits, variables, parentheses, squares, roots, π, comparison symbols, etc.
Form a valid expression
The graph updates immediately according to the expression
After collapsing the auxiliary keyboard the expressions and graph stay unchanged
features.expected: An expression entered with the auxiliary keyboard must be parsed correctly and drive the graph; after collapsing the keyboard the expression and graph stay unchanged.

features.name: Auxiliary keyboard + function input
steps: Create an expression
Open the auxiliary keyboard
Enter sin, exponents, parentheses, and digits through categories such as "functions/ABC"
Construct a function such as f(x)=x+5·sin(10x)
Verify curve generation
Modify one of the parameters
The curve updates in real time while existing geometric objects continue to exist
features.expected: The function curve built via the auxiliary keyboard is generated correctly; changing parameters updates it in real time; existing geometric objects continue to exist.

features.name: Cross-object input with the auxiliary keyboard
steps: Create a function expression
Then create a table and edit values
Use the auxiliary keyboard to switch between expression and table-value input
Modify function parameters and table data
The corresponding curve and data points update separately
The current document state is preserved when the keyboard is closed and reopened
features.expected: The auxiliary keyboard switches normally between expression and table input; after modification the curve and data points update separately; the document state is preserved after closing and reopening the keyboard.

exclusions.feature:
Real-time multi-user collaboration
Exclude multi-user real-time cursors, simultaneous editing, conflict merging, and online collaboration rooms
exclusions.reason: Depends on WebSocket / Presence / multi-account infrastructure and is not suitable as a single-agent web-reproduction benchmark

exclusions.feature:
Sharing permissions and public collaboration
Exclude inviting members, link permissions, owner/editor permissions, and public publishing
exclusions.reason: It belongs to the cloud account and permission system rather than the core geometric-construction capability

exclusions.feature:
Login / registration / account management
Exclude account registration, password recovery, third-party login, and user security settings
exclusions.reason: Without a real identity service it cannot be reproduced reliably and it does not test a geometry agent's capabilities

exclusions.feature:
The full advanced capabilities of the Graphing Calculator
Geometry is not required to reproduce all statistics, distributions, inference, and advanced list functions of the Desmos Calculator
exclusions.reason: Although Geometry embeds algebra/graphing capabilities, the benchmark should keep only the representative expression capabilities that support geometric construction; retained surface: f01 point–segment dependent construction, f05 geometric intersection dependency chain, f07 geometry overlaid with functions

exclusions.feature:
The complete set of mathematical functions
Exclude implementing every statistics function, probability distribution, hypothesis test, special function, and edge-case syntax one by one
exclusions.reason: It would turn the benchmark into a math-parser compatibility test rather than an end-to-end Geometry agent test

exclusions.feature:
3D Calculator
Exclude 3D points, surfaces, 3D rotation, the 3D camera, and 3D geometry
exclusions.reason: It is a separate Desmos product and is outside the scope of Geometry planar geometry

exclusions.feature:
Desmos Classroom / Activity Builder
Exclude teacher classrooms, student sessions, activity creation, class codes, and assignment management
exclusions.reason: It requires a full education platform, multiple accounts, and classroom data

exclusions.feature:
The full version-history backend
Exclude cross-version diffs, restore-to-any-point, and full cloud revision history
exclusions.reason: The benchmark only needs to verify the final visible state after saving and reopening

exclusions.feature:
Cloud photo-asset management
Exclude the cloud photo library, photo CDN, remote-URL permissions, and cross-account photo sharing
exclusions.reason: This benchmark only needs to select a local image and use it in Geometry

exclusions.feature:
Full replication of the Geometry gallery / examples
Exclude all official Equilateral Triangle, Euler Line, Pythagorean Theorem, and other gallery content
exclusions.reason: It is a content dataset rather than the Geometry editor itself; the official Gallery does contain many examples, but there is no need to copy them one by one. Desmos

exclusions.feature:
Exhaustively cover all Geometry Commands
All parameter forms and exceptional inputs of every intersection(), glider(), radius(), etc. are not tested one by one
exclusions.reason: Choosing representative intersection, distance, and area operations is enough to cover object references and dependency computation

exclusions.feature:
Extreme numerical-precision consistency
Bit-for-bit agreement with Desmos on floating-point error, intersection approximation, curve sampling, and extremely small-scale constructions is excluded
exclusions.reason: Extremely costly to implement and does not affect the agent's main operation and state-management capabilities

exclusions.feature:
Pixel-perfect rendering consistency
Curve anti-aliasing, fonts, control-point size, fill transparency, and line width are not required to match the official app pixel by pixel
exclusions.reason: It should test semantic structure, dynamic relationships, and user-visible functional results rather than a renderer copy

exclusions.feature:
Advanced accessibility hardware and assistive technology
Exclude Braille, deep screen-reader adaptation, voice/audio navigation, and dedicated assistive-hardware integration; the in-page Desmos math keyboard is not excluded
exclusions.reason: The in-page math keyboard is a core input component and should be implemented; only capabilities that genuinely depend on extra assistive hardware or a dedicated accessibility runtime are excluded

exclusions.feature:
Full OS-level IME compatibility
Reproducing all physical keyboard layouts, IMEs, mobile soft keyboards, and system shortcut differences is not required
exclusions.reason: The benchmark only requires the in-page math keyboard and ordinary text-keyboard input to work correctly

exclusions.feature:
Full mobile gestures
Exclude touch-specific dragging, pinch zoom, mobile keyboards, and native app behavior
exclusions.reason: The benchmark fixes the desktop web environment

exclusions.feature:
Export / print infrastructure
Exclude high-quality PDF/SVG/print layouts, printer adaptation, and browser print differences
exclusions.reason: It belongs to output infrastructure and is not the core of geometric modeling

exclusions.feature:
Community content / public search
Exclude searching other users' public Geometry, community works, and recommendation algorithms
exclusions.reason: Depends on an external content database and search index

exclusions.feature:
Full internationalization
Exclude all language UIs, RTL, all locale number formats, and keyboard layouts
exclusions.reason: The benchmark only needs to fix a single UI language

exclusions.feature:
Help center / tutorial videos
Exclude help documents, tutorial videos, customer-service entries, and tutorial content
exclusions.reason: It belongs to a supporting content system and is not a geometry-editor feature

exclusions.feature:
Third-party embedding
Exclude LMS, Google Classroom, external website embeds, and third-party authorization
exclusions.reason: Depends on an external platform, which is not conducive to a stable, repeatable benchmark
